summary: Stone fire tower on Massaemet Mountain above Shelburne Falls; built from 1909, in service 1911; still a seasonally staffed state lookout per 2016 visit reports and a 2025 trail guide.

facts.design: Stone tower with a 10 by 10 foot wooden cab, upgraded several times

access.note: Public trail to the tower; the wooden cab is locked when not in use, but visitors may still climb 72 spiral steps (2025 trail guide)

visit.trail_note: Tower Trail climbs 1.25 miles from Route 2 at Halligan Avenue; the yellow-blazed Big Tree Trail is an easier alternative

facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

events.note: Construction began in 1909 per the register; the register says the tower went into service in 1911
A November 1911 newspaper says the State Forestry Commission set up the station in August of the year before, i.e. August 1910
Went into service, per the register; a 2025 trail guide repeats 1911
Village citizens owned the tower and a committee controlled it; the state sought to take it over
Donald G. Wood appointed observer after Nelson Woodward resigned, having served about 26 years
2016 register visit report: a seasonal observer on duty from late March to early September

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says construction began in 1909 and the tower went into service in 1911; a November 1911 newspaper dates the state station to the previous August (1910). The brief's 1909 build year is kept as the start of construction.
Register gives 63 ft (19.2 m); the 1940 Massachusetts Geodetic Survey station description gives 60 ft. Facts use the register's 63 ft; the story reports both.
The summit is called Massaemet, Massamet or Massaemett in these sources, and Bald Mountain in the 1940 station description. Story uses Massaemet.

notes_for_editor: Four pages read: the NHLR register entry (2016 visit reports include the seasonal observer), the Forest Lookouts Mount Massaemet page (newspaper history 1911 to 1969 and the 1940 geodetic description), the 2025 Trailspotting trail guide (active service, cab locked, 72 steps open), and the Franklin Land Trust trail page. No 2026 source confirms current staffing; the 2025 guide does not describe staffing, so facts.staffing rests on the 2016 report. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1940 geodetic station description that calls the summit Bald Mountain; the other sources use Massaemet. Brief's 1909 build year is kept as construction start. Record's elevation 478.2 m matches the register's 1,569 ft (478 m). No photos added. The register's 'Tom Ashton photo' and '1920 photo' credits were not read for license terms.
